label: input token t during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter t as input during the original phase. On dev it fires on every original-phase t (precision 1.0) and nowhere else in the original phase. It almost never fires on other letters (stray weak firings on m and k). It never fires at the <DEL> step. In the copy phase it is nearly silent: the only exception is a weak echo (about 0.14 of max) when a fed-back t is input at recall_idx 1, i.e. t was orig(0). That echo makes up the misses, which hold 0.3% of mass. Activations are fairly uniform, about 0.6-0.8 of max. The top examples are all a t that is the last original token just before <DEL>, and a t at position 0 sits at about 0.83. Repeated (non-first) occurrences of t are over-represented in the lowest activation quartile, so they are somewhat weaker but still active. Sequence length, neighbouring tokens and digit count have little effect.

issues: Small imprecision: the explanation describes the recall_idx-1 'echo' (a fed-back t at recall_idx 1) as if it happens every time. It actually fires on only about 11% of those steps. Adding (recall_idx==1)&(in_tok==t) to the predicate gives 15k+ false positives and drops test F1 to 0.936. These echoes are too weak (about 0.14-0.17 of max) and too inconsistent to belong in the predicate, so this does not refute the label.

Everything else checks out on the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.981, F1 0.991, mass recall 0.997, zero false positives. It never fires at <DEL>. About 0.3% of activation mass is in the copy phase. The only other tokens it fires on are m (92) and k (45), all weak. The top examples are t as the last original token at about 0.96-1.0 of max. A t at position 0 sits at about 0.83. Nearly all misses are the weak echo class, all of them in the lowest activation quartile.
